sections.h2: How is Tattnall County laid out for a home seller?
sections.html:
Tattnall is a farm-and-river county in southeast Georgia. Reidsville holds the courthouse and Glennville is the biggest town. Wikipedia gives December 5, 1801 as the founding date, credits Josiah Tattnall as namesake, and measures 488 square miles with 479 of land.

Three river basins split the land. The Ohoopee drains the west, the Canoochee takes the northeast strip between Cobbtown and east of Reidsville, and the Altamaha collects the southeast and southwest corners. Municipalities are Cobbtown, Collins, Glennville, Manassas and Reidsville, and Mendes is a census-designated place. U.S. 25 shares a roadway with U.S. 301, U.S. 280 runs with State Route 30, and eight counties touch the boundary: Candler, Evans, Liberty, Long, Wayne, Appling, Toombs and Emanuel.

The county's own website devotes pages to agriculture and the Vidalia onion. Census counts fell 10.5%, from 25,520 residents in 2010 to 22,842 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate of 24,376 shows a rebound.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Tattnall County housing?
sections.html:
Owner-held homes have a midpoint value of $140,000 for 2020-2024, and owners fill 71.0% of occupied housing. That tops the $117,100 to $120,200 range for Talbot, Terrell and Sumter counties, while middle gross rent is a lower $699.

sections.h2: Who does what in Tattnall County tax administration?
sections.html:
Billing and collection happen at 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, with P.O. Box 920 for mail. The county's payment portal lists the phone as 912-557-6736 and the hours as 8 to 5 on weekdays.

  • Tax commissioner: ad valorem tax, mobile homes, public utilities, timber, and vehicle tags.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: five members chosen by the county commissioners, with a chief appraiser directing the staff.
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury to hear disputed values.
  • County commissioners and school board: budgets that drive the millage.

The county's general information page says Tattnall's assessors, rather than the commissioner, receive returns. It adds that a state levy cannot exceed one fourth of a mill.

The commissioner is elected every four years, and the county notes that this is one of the four elected positions created by the original Georgia Constitution. The county adds that cities benefit from the vehicle and mobile home taxes the office collects, so ask which accounts attach to your address.

sections.h2: How do returns, homestead and use-based assessments work in Tattnall County?
sections.html:
A taxpayer holding property on January 1 files a return between then and April 1. The first one renews itself at last year's final value, so a new filing is needed only for added property, improvements or a different value you want on record.

Homestead covers the house you own and live in, with paperwork going to the assessors' office. The assessors' own page sets April 1 as the deadline and says Tattnall offers no local homestead exemptions beyond the statewide ones. The FAQ asks for applications before March 1, so filing early avoids a miss.

Programs described in the county FAQ:

  • Preferential agricultural property: assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40, with a ten year commitment.
  • Conservation use: valued by current use for bona fide farm or forest land, also ten years.
  • Environmentally sensitive and residential transitional land: current-use value, with applications taken January 2 through April 1.
  • Standing timber: no tax until it is sold or cut, then 100 percent of fair market value.

Before listing enrolled land, ask the assessors what the covenant means for the next owner.

sections.h2: How do Tattnall County assessors arrive at a value?
sections.html:
The county defines fair market value as the price a knowledgeable buyer and a willing seller would agree on in an arm's length sale, fixed as of January 1. Assessed value is 40 percent of that, and each mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Three methods appear in the FAQ. Cost starts from replacement cost less depreciation and adds land, market compares nearby sales, and income capitalizes net rent on commercial or rental property. Business equipment and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent too. If you have a recent arm's length sale, hold on to the contract and settlement statement as your best market evidence.

sections.h2: What is Tattnall County's due date?
sections.html:
Read your statement. The state fact sheet for Tattnall treats December 20 as the official date, lets a county switch to December 1, November 15 or installments, and gives each taxpayer 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts.

The online portal offers a property tax option, and the office line is 912-557-6736. Mobile homes follow their own state schedule: a location permit within 30 days of permanent placement, then a return and permit renewal each year from January 1 to April 1.

One credit is not guaranteed. The Homeowners Tax Relief Grant shows up only in years the General Assembly funds it, and the county warns that bills climb when the money is absent. Ask what credit, if any, is on your statement.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Tattnall County valuation?
sections.html:
Once the assessors change a value, a written answer is due within 45 days of the notice date, and the county treats a late one as invalid.

Your reason has to be taxability, uniformity or value, and a gripe about the tax itself does not count. The assessors review first. If the number stands, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, and either side may continue to Tattnall County Superior Court. Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization if you choose it at filing.

The county stresses that assessors read the market and do not invent prices. If a recent contract differs from the county's number, attach it to the appeal.

sections.h2: What happens when Tattnall County tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels go to a courthouse sale. One was held Tuesday, June 7, 2022, at 10 a.m. in the second floor Commissioners Meeting room. An auction caps a long delinquency, so an owner behind has choices well before then.

Get written payoffs by year, and for a mobile home confirm the decal and permit are settled. The county FAQ charges tax to whoever owns the property on January 1, and the settlement statement is where you and the buyer divide the year. Any earlier balance is then paid by the title company out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Tattnall County property tax?
faqs.a: At the tax commissioner's office, 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, or through the county's online payment portal. The phone is 912-557-6736 and the office keeps hours of 8 to 5 on weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the homestead cutoff in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: April 1 per the Board of Tax Assessors page. The county FAQ mentions March 1, so file before March to be safe. The assessors' office takes the form.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to appeal in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date of the notice, in writing. Late appeals are invalid.

faqs.q: Does Tattnall County have its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Tax Assessors page says none are offered locally, so owners apply for the statewide exemptions.

faqs.q: Is timber taxed in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: Yes, when it is sold or harvested. The tax uses 100 percent of fair market value, and the FAQ covers lump sum, unit price and owner harvest sales.
